3. The proposed ternary kernel does give an explicit degeneration

The kernel idea is mathematically valid and yields more than a dimension calculation. Its fourth piece is, however, a binary boundary product.

Set
$R_e=\mathbb Q[x,y,z]_e,\qquad
S_e=\mathbb Q[y,z]_e,\qquad
D_e=\binom{e+2}{2},$
and define
$\sigma_e:R_e^3\to R_{e+1},
\qquad
\sigma_e(v_1,v_2,v_3)=xv_1+yv_2+zv_3.$
Let $K_e=\ker\sigma_e$.

For $e\ge1$, introduce
$i_1(h)=(-yh,xh,0),\qquad
i_2(h)=(-zh,0,xh),\qquad
i_3(q)=(0,-zq,yq),$
where $h\in R_{e-1}$ and $q\in S_{e-1}$.

The filtration
$0
\subset
i_1(R_{e-1})\oplus i_2(R_{e-1})
\subset
K_e
\subset
R_e^3$
has successive pieces
$R_{e-1}^{\oplus2},\qquad S_{e-1},\qquad R_{e+1}.
\tag{8}$
Multiplication by any $A\in R_a$ acts by $A$ on the free pieces, by $A(0,y,z)$ on the binary piece, and by $A$ on the final quotient. Thus the compatibility holds uniformly for every left input.


Explicit encoders and decoders

For $w\in R_{e+1}$, define coefficient-shift maps
$s_1(w)=\frac{w-w(0,y,z)}x,
\quad
s_2(w)=\frac{w(0,y,z)-w(0,0,z)}y,
\quad
s_3(w)=\frac{w(0,0,z)}z.$
These divisions are exact shifts of monomial indices.

Given
$h_1,h_2\in R_{e-1},\quad q\in S_{e-1},\quad w\in R_{e+1},$
encode
$\begin{aligned}
E_1&=-yh_1-zh_2+\varepsilon^2s_1(w),\\
E_2&=xh_1-\varepsilon zq+\varepsilon^2s_2(w),\\
E_3&=xh_2+\varepsilon yq+\varepsilon^2s_3(w).
\end{aligned}
\tag{9}$
Compute the three products $W_j=AE_j$. Decode
$\begin{aligned}
U_1&=\frac{W_2-W_2(0,y,z)}x,\\
U_2&=\frac{W_3-W_3(0,y,z)}x,\\
Q&=\varepsilon^{-1}
\frac{W_3(0,y,z)-W_3(0,0,z)}y,\\
W&=\varepsilon^{-2}(xW_1+yW_2+zW_3).
\end{aligned}
\tag{10}$
Then
$U_1\equiv Ah_1,\qquad
U_2\equiv Ah_2,\qquad
Q\equiv A(0,y,z)q
\pmod{\varepsilon},$
and
$W=Aw$
exactly.

The negative parameter powers cancel. Every decoded output is polynomial in $\varepsilon$, of degree at most two. All coefficient maps use $0,\pm1$, restrictions, shifts and additions. They take $O((a+e+1)^2)$ coefficient operations, with paid logarithmic-bit indices.

This proves a genuine shared-left degeneration
$3P^{(3)}_{a,e}
\;\rightsquigarrow\;
2P^{(3)}_{a,e-1}
\oplus_1
\widetilde P^{(2)}_{a,e-1}
\oplus_1
P^{(3)}_{a,e+1},
\tag{11}$
where the binary term uses the restricted left polynomial $A(0,y,z)$. Transposition supplies the dual.
